Case Study

The Attitude Shift

Analyze how one person’s visible behavior changes the team around it.

GROUPS OF 3–5
Scenario: A five-person team is preparing a client update. Early in the week, Jordan raises two risks and offers to help. After the manager changes the deadline, Jordan begins saying, “It does not matter, they will change it again.” Jordan stops volunteering status updates, responds to questions with short answers, and jokes that the project is “already doomed.” Within two days, two teammates stop raising issues because they expect sarcasm. Another waits until the last minute to report a data problem. The client update goes out with an avoidable error.

Triad Practice

Speaker, Listener, Observer

Rotate roles every four minutes. Use a provided scenario or a non-sensitive real work challenge.

Speaker

Describe the work challenge clearly. Focus on context, not a long backstory.

Listener

Listen without solving. Ask at least one clarifying question and use a confirmation statement.

Observer

Watch only for observable behaviors on the rubric. Give behavioral feedback.

RotationSpeaker, Listener, Observer. Rotate every 4 minutes until everyone has used each role.
Listener mustAsk at least one clarifying question and use one confirmation statement.
Observer mustUse the rubric below and give feedback only on what was seen or heard.
Optional work scenario: A teammate tells you they cannot finish a deliverable by the agreed time because a dependency arrived late. They are frustrated and unsure what to do next.
Observer criterionObserved?Notes
Did not interrupt
Paraphrased accurately
Asked a clarifying question
Checked the need before offering advice
Confirmed the next step
Tone stayed neutral

Section 4

Collaborative Conflict

Disagreement is information. Escalation is a choice.

Breakout Role-Play

Resolve the Work, Not the Person

Use the four-step framework to move a real work problem forward.

PAIRS

1 · Shared outcome

What are both sides trying to protect?

2 · Facts & constraints

What is true? What limits the options?

3 · Options

Generate at least two workable paths.

4 · Confirm

Who will do what, and by when?

PracticeUse the four-step framework in a 6-minute role-play.
ReplaySwitch roles or replay with improved wording.
Success measureSurface the facts and tradeoff, offer options, then confirm a next step.

When I Feel Myself Getting Defensive...

Capstone

Project Phoenix

Use the course skills together to protect the outcome and the team experience.

Capstone Brief

Project Phoenix: Customer Self-Service Portal Launch

Your team is preparing a new customer self-service portal for a Friday 3:00 p.m. go-live. New information will arrive in rounds.

TEAMS OF 3–5

What is being launched?

A new customer self-service portal that lets customers view account status, download statements, and submit service requests online.

Shared outcome: a stable, understandable launch with accurate data, ready support, clear customer communication, and visible ownership.
Account Status
Statements
Service Requests
Operations

Owns go-live coordination, workflow readiness, testing coordination, and launch stability.

Customer Support

Owns launch staffing, support readiness, FAQs in use, and the first wave of customer questions.

Finance

Owns the account and billing data that feeds the portal and validates the final data file.

Communications

Owns the customer announcement, final screenshots, FAQs, and launch messaging.

Current conditions: Finance’s account-data feed is running late. Communications needs confirmed features and screenshots by noon Thursday to finalize the customer announcement and FAQ. Customer Support has a staffing gap during the Friday launch window. A senior stakeholder wants to add an account-reporting feature before launch.
Your jobProtect the portal launch, not create a perfect technical project plan.
Keep in viewCustomer experience, data accuracy, support readiness, communication, and ownership.
How it worksStay with the same team. Each round adds information that may change your plan.
Round 1

Build the Team Response

Create an initial operating picture for the portal launch before the scenario changes.

9 MIN BREAKOUT
Define successWhat must be true at Friday go-live?
Prioritize riskWhich two current conditions most threaten that outcome?
Make it actionableName who needs communication today and assign one immediate ownership action.
Be ready to share: your communication sentence first, then why your team chose it.
Twist 1

The Missed Handoff

An avoidable error appears. Respond without turning accountability into blame.

New information: Finance discovers that the account-billing data file sent yesterday was the wrong version. The portal validation process must be rerun. Rework will take 90 minutes, and nobody is sure who approved the file before it was shared.
First priorityRecover the launch. Do not spend the breakout investigating who made the mistake.
ProduceOne accountability sentence that states the issue and next step without blaming a person.
Fix the handoffDefine one immediate process change that prevents another wrong-file release before Friday.
Twist 2

New Request, Same Deadline

Make the tradeoff visible when a high-visibility request competes with the launch.

Stakeholder request: A senior stakeholder asks to add account reporting before Friday because leadership would like the feature included at launch. Operations says adding it now requires another test cycle and risks Friday’s go-live. Finance is still recovering from the wrong-file issue. Communications is waiting on final screenshots and features. Customer Support is already short-staffed for the launch window.
Use the conflict frameworkShared outcome, facts and constraints, options, confirmation.
You may recommendNo, not now, or a reduced version. “Team player” does not automatically mean yes.
ProduceAn exact stakeholder response and an internal decision about what changes, if anything.
Team Board

Make the Plan Visible

Build one operating picture that a person joining the portal launch late could understand in less than one minute.

5 MIN BUILD
Your board should account for: the account-data feed, the wrong billing file, screenshots due Thursday noon, the Customer Support staffing gap, and the account-reporting request.
Capstone Debrief

What Made the Team Stronger?

Debrief the team behaviors, not the technical quality of the portal plan.

Look back across the full simulation: the late data feed, the wrong billing file, the staffing gap, the communications deadline, and the account-reporting request.
